\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بالتالي} (bi-t-tālī)}{بالتالي (bi-t-tālī)}]{\ar{بالتالي} (bi-t-tālī) — consequently}

\label{lesson:AR-C374-bi-t-tali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to back down, then the Arabic for to resolve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بالتالي}}
\textbf{\ar{بالتالي}} — \emph{bi-t-tālī} — \textquotedblleft{}consequently\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الطريق} \ar{مغلقا،} \ar{بالتالي} \ar{تأخر} \ar{الجميع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna aṭ-ṭarīq mughlaqan, bi-t-tālī taʾakhkhara al-jamīʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The road was closed; consequently everyone was late.
\end{quote}

Usually with \ar{و}: \ar{وبالتالي}, and as a result.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بالتالي}} (\emph{bi-t-tālī}) joins \emph{bi-}, \textquotedblleft{}by\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{at-tālī}, \textquotedblleft{}the one that follows\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{t-l-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to follow\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Literally, by what follows.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-t-tālī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-t-tālī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna aṭ-ṭarīq mughlaqan, bi-t-tālī taʾakhkhara al-jamīʿ.} — The road was closed; consequently everyone was late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to back down, then the Arabic for to resolve, then say \emph{bi-t-tālī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بالتالي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Consequently\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب} (li-hādhā as-sabab)}{لهذا السبب (li-hādhā as-sabab)}]{\ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب} (li-hādhā as-sabab) — for this reason}

\label{lesson:AR-C374-li-hadha-as-sabab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to resolve, then the Arabic for consequently.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب}}
\textbf{\ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب}} — \emph{li-hādhā as-sabab} — \textquotedblleft{}for this reason\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{الجو} \ar{ممطرا،} \ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب} \ar{بقينا} \ar{في} \ar{المنزل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna al-jaww mumṭiran, li-hādhā as-sabab baqīnā fī al-manzil.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The weather was rainy; for this reason we stayed at home.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب}} (\emph{li-hādhā as-sabab}) is a phrase: \emph{li-}, \textquotedblleft{}for\textquotedblright{}, \emph{hādhā}, \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{as-sabab}, \textquotedblleft{}the reason\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-b-b}, \textquotedblleft{}a rope; a means to an end\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-hādhā as-sabab}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-hādhā as-sabab}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna al-jaww mumṭiran, li-hādhā as-sabab baqīnā fī al-manzil.} — The weather was rainy; for this reason we stayed at home.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to resolve, then the Arabic for consequently, then say \emph{li-hādhā as-sabab} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{لهذا} \ar{السبب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}For this reason\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بما} \ar{أن} (bi-mā anna)}{بما أن (bi-mā anna)}]{\ar{بما} \ar{أن} (bi-mā anna) — seeing that; since}

\label{lesson:AR-C374-bi-ma-anna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for consequently, then the Arabic for for this reason.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بما} \ar{أن}}
\textbf{\ar{بما} \ar{أن}} — \emph{bi-mā anna} — \textquotedblleft{}seeing that; since\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بما} \ar{أن} \ar{اليوم} \ar{عطلة،} \ar{سننام} \ar{متأخرين}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bi-mā anna al-yawm ʿuṭla, sa-nanāmu mutaʾakhkhirīn.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Seeing that today is a holiday, we will sleep late.
\end{quote}

It gives a reason both speakers already accept.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بما} \ar{أن}} (\emph{bi-mā anna}) is built from three native Arabic function words: \emph{bi-}, \textquotedblleft{}by\textquotedblright{}, \emph{mā}, \textquotedblleft{}what\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{anna}, \textquotedblleft{}that\textquotedblright{}. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-mā anna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-mā anna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bi-mā anna al-yawm ʿuṭla, sa-nanāmu mutaʾakhkhirīn.} — Seeing that today is a holiday, we will sleep late.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for consequently, then the Arabic for for this reason, then say \emph{bi-mā anna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بما} \ar{أن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Seeing that; since\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حيث} \ar{إن} (ḥaythu inna)}{حيث إن (ḥaythu inna)}]{\ar{حيث} \ar{إن} (ḥaythu inna) — given that}

\label{lesson:AR-C374-haythu-inna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for for this reason, then the Arabic for seeing that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حيث} \ar{إن}}
\textbf{\ar{حيث} \ar{إن}} — \emph{ḥaythu inna} — \textquotedblleft{}given that\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{حيث} \ar{إن} \ar{الطريق} \ar{طويل،} \ar{سنخرج} \ar{مبكرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḥaythu inna aṭ-ṭarīq ṭawīl, sa-nakhruju mubakkiran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Given that the road is long, we will leave early.
\end{quote}

Formal; in speech \ar{بما} \ar{أن} or \ar{لأن}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حيث} \ar{إن}} (\emph{ḥaythu inna}) joins two native Arabic particles: \emph{ḥaythu}, \textquotedblleft{}where\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{inna}, \textquotedblleft{}indeed, truly\textquotedblright{}. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaythu inna}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaythu inna}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥaythu inna aṭ-ṭarīq ṭawīl, sa-nakhruju mubakkiran.} — Given that the road is long, we will leave early.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for for this reason, then the Arabic for seeing that, then say \emph{ḥaythu inna} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حيث} \ar{إن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Given that\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لكي} (li-kay)}{لكي (li-kay)}]{\ar{لكي} (li-kay) — in order to}

\label{lesson:AR-C374-li-kay}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for seeing that, then the Arabic for given that.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لكي}}
\textbf{\ar{لكي}} — \emph{li-kay} — \textquotedblleft{}in order to\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يدرس} \ar{أخي} \ar{كل} \ar{ليلة} \ar{لكي} \ar{ينجح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yadrusu akhī kulla layla li-kay yanjaḥa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother studies every night in order to pass.
\end{quote}

The verb after it takes the subjunctive: \ar{لكي} \ar{ينجح}, \emph{li-kay yanjaḥa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لكي}} (\emph{li-kay}) joins the native Arabic particles \emph{li-}, \textquotedblleft{}for\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{kay}, \textquotedblleft{}so that\textquotedblright{}, which learners met on its own earlier. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-kay}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{li-kay}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yadrusu akhī kulla layla li-kay yanjaḥa.} — My brother studies every night in order to pass.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for seeing that, then the Arabic for given that, then say \emph{li-kay} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{لكي} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}In order to\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
